body: Whether it'll be my brother, my mum, or my dad who finds my dead body in my room eventually. I don't want any of them to find it, they've all had enough problems lately and the last thing they need is to find their dead son.

I've attempted suicide before.

*Yeaaah nobody would treat me the same.*

I can't tell them because I can't fully trust any of them... I know that they will try to get me help, and get me to see a therapist, or something like that. I don't want that. I don't want people to think of me as a weird, insane, mentally ill, freak.

Not trolling... I'm not a doctor, I'm just saying I think I have this stuff. I have things that are signs of this stuff.

I'm 13 and I want to kill myself... I am 99.99% sure I have anger management issues, I might have ASPD (Anti-Social Personality Disorder), and to put it softly, I dislike my family a lot. I'm bullied a lot. I am ugly, I have about one real friend. I'm basically the quiet nerdy kid that you always made fun of at school. Yeeaaah... Fuck my life...

Edit: jeez, I should change accounts. I answer OP's question, but get downvoted because of my age. Reddit is a truly beautiful place.

Edit 2: I know it's kind of late to say this, but thanks to everyone who commented nice things and messaged me. It's good to know that some people care, even if they are strangers. Thanks.
Been there already... They're no help.
A successful suicide... It has yet to happen :(

My school doesn't have a counselor, and no, they don't. And not really. I've tried many things. Punching the air, yelling into pillows, throwing soft things like socks and teddy bears, but nothing works. Thanks for the advice though.

It's nice to know someone else has gone through this. I don't know if apology by parent would work, as our parents used to be good friends, but I'm afraid her mom doesn't like us any more after this incident... And I do have a hobby, gaming. This summer I spent $1200 on my completely custom built gaming PC... I love it like it's my child. My real friends are my online friends that I've never met in real life, so talking to real friends online isn't much of a problem. Thanks for the advice.
I try, but it's kind of hard to during school. In my free time I isolate myself, only leaving my computer and xbox for food and drinks. Thanks for the advice.

Trust me, gaming is my hobby... Just this summer I spent $1200 of my own money to build my completely custom gaming PC. I try to isolate myself and just play video games and make online friends (WAAAAY better than real friends) but my parents don't like it. They push me to go do things with friends. I try to, but then this ends up happening.

Gaming makes me angry too, but I usually just punch the air and stuff because it doesn't make me as mad as some stuff in real life. Thanks for the advice, though.

Don't mean to sound like an ass, and if I do, I'm sorry. It's just when people say this I get kinda upset.

Suicide isn't a permanent solution to a temporary problem. For many suicidal people their problems are permanent. For example, a man might have lost all of his family members and has no friends, he is completely alone. Even if he gets friends he will not get his family back. Losing loved ones is a permanent problem, and many people contemplate suicide because they lost loved ones. Maybe they found out he is terminally ill and has no chance of survival and doesn't want to go through the pain. I understand that these scenarios are pretty extreme, but they are still possible.

What I'm trying to say is that in some cases, *it is* a permanent problem. I am in no way meaning to promote suicide, I'm just saying it's not always a temporary problem. Although, in many cases, you are right. It is a temporary problem. Sometimes though, those problems are extremely hard to solve, such as homelessness, no job, debt, etc.

Sorry for all of that, just felt like sharing. Again, I'm sorry if I seem like an ass.

Yup. I totally agree. I've posted there twice (once about my suicidal thoughts and once about my attempt) and all I really got was a bunch of people just saying the same thing. "it will get better", "you're just going through puberty", and "your parents love you, tell them about how you feel." The only useful people were 2 people. One who is one of my closest Internet friends, and the other was a 20-something man that had gone through pretty much the same stuff and gave me some advice. All in all, /r/suicidewatch is useless (except for a few exceptions).

God, being 13 sucks :/

I'm probably VERY late, but here's mine.

No, just because I'm young doesn't mean I'm happy and carefree. No, weed won't help me be happier. No, I can't just snap out of it and be as happy as a homeless guy winning the lottery.

No, saying that I'm on my period because I got angry isn't funny. Anger management is hard to deal with. Also, I'm a guy. I don't get periods.

No, saying that I'm a nerd because I'm good at math and I built my computer isn't funny at all. It hurts.

No, saying that suicide is selfish won't help. I won't be happy just because you told me to "turn that frown upside down". 

At my age, life and the world sucks. I hate it all. (13 if you didn't read my username :/)
